literatureReviews.resourceInsights:
- A user interface (UI) which adapts (changes) its layout and elements to the needs of the user or context and is similarly alterable by each user.
- Advantages: AUIs help users access the most important information quickly, reducing confusion and streamlining interaction.
- Disadvantages: The main challenge lies in accurately determining a user’s goal to adapt the interface effectively.
#1 Adaptive Presentation (ex. Basic users might see simplified content, while advanced users get more detailed information)
#2 Adaptive Navigation (ex. Basic users could be guided with help prompts, creating a more curated experience.)

User Proficiency Estimation (determining user's needs)
- by Simple Metrics (attached to their identity in the system, ex. how much time has elapsed since log in)
- by Advanced Analytics (a larger picture of how the user interacts with the system, ex. how frequent do they visit, which buttons do they press etc.)

literatureReviews.resourceName: The impact of educational live action role-playing games on social–emotional competence: a mixed-method study with Chinese college students
literatureReviews.resourceInsights: Studiul analizează efectul jocurilor educaționale de tip LARP asupra competenței socio-emoționale la studenți chinezi, folosind o metodă mixtă (chestionar + interviuri). Au participat 84 de studenți, împărțiți în grup experimental și control, iar grupul experimental a jucat LARP timp de 8 săptămâni (2–5 ore/săptămână). Rezultatele arată creșteri semnificative în „Implicare cu ceilalți”, „Colaborare” și „Deschidere”, față de grupul control. Cele mai mari îmbunătățiri apar la asertivitate, sociabilitate, empatie, cooperare, toleranță și curiozitate. Interviurile confirmă că role-play-ul și sarcinile de echipă oferă un cadru „sigur” pentru exersarea comunicării și a înțelegerii celorlalți. Autorii recomandă scenarii bine scrise, contexte imersive și facilitatori (DM) pregătiți pentru integrarea LARP-urilor în programe universitare.

literatureReviews.resourceName: Collaborative learning through augmented reality role playing
literatureReviews.resourceInsights:
The study argues that handheld AR games can create authentic, engaging contexts for collaborative learning because players move through the real world and communicate naturally. 
In the first game generation (Environmental Detectives), collaboration within teams was strong, but collaboration between teams was limited. 
To strengthen broader collaboration, the second generation introduced time dependence, cascading events, and especially distinct roles. 
Distinct roles give each player different information and capabilities (e.g., different kinds of data/samples), making information exchange necessary to solve the investigation. 
As a result, these mechanics increase positive interdependence and individual accountability, leading to more meaningful collaboration that supports a more realistic inquiry process. 
The authors also stress that role “overlap” must be calibrated: too much overlap reduces the need to collaborate, while too little overlap reduces shared ground for discussion.

literatureReviews.resourceName: Requirements Analysis of Presence:Insights from a RPG Game
literatureReviews.resourceInsights:
1. Presence comes from coherence, not technology. Users feel "they are there" not because of graphics, but because the virtual world's rules are consistent with their real-world expectations. In a real-world RPG, this is solved naturally - the city, weather, and people are already real.
2. Character identity is the emotional entry point. Players treat their RPG character as an extension of their real self, not just a tool. The character creation process is not onboarding - it is the moment where the user decides whether to emotionally invest in the experience.
3. Sociability must be structured, not left to emerge organically. Guilds and ranking systems naturally encourage interaction. Without clear social structure, players do not interact with each other even when sharing the same physical space.
4. Responsiveness is perceived, not just measured. The same system can feel fast to some users and slow to others, depending on how well they understand the interface. Design must always make the next step predictable for the user.
5. User control directly increases engagement. The more control users have over content and experience, the deeper their involvement. Allowing players to create quests for others transforms consumers into contributors.
6. Navigation must be context-aware, not standardized. Casual users want to explore; advanced users want efficiency. A good system offers both simultaneously - detailed map on mobile, quick tracker on smartwatch, turn-by-turn directions on AR glasses.
7. Too much realism breaks the experience. Excessive physical realism without appropiate feedback disrupts immersion. On AR especially, overlays must appear at exactly the right moment - never too early, never delayed.

1. The avatar becomes the player's real-world identity
Players don't just control a character — they adopt its traits and behaviors (Proteus Effect). In a real-life RPG where you are the character, this effect is amplified. The role a user picks will influence how they actually behave in the real world during gameplay.
2. There are 4 types of player-avatar relationships to design for
Banks (2015) defines four ways users relate to their character: as a tool (Object), as a self-extension (Me), as an interconnected but separate entity (Symbiote), or as an independent being (Other). For your project, the goal is to push users toward Me or Symbiote — the role must feel like it genuinely belongs to them.
3. Character design naturally communicates abilities
A well-designed character visually justifies its skills without needing a tutorial. If a character looks like a rogue, users instinctively know what they can do. On AR glasses especially, the visible role (costume, badge, rank) must instantly communicate who you are in the world.
4. Backstory deepens identity projection
When a character has its own story, users identify with it more deeply. Each role — thief, merchant, explorer, guide — should come with a short origin story at onboarding to emotionally anchor the user to their character.
5. Character form guides player behavior
The physical design of an avatar determines what actions feel natural. A character that looks aggressive encourages attacking; one that looks stealthy encourages hiding. Each class in your game should have a visual design that immediately suggests its associated playstyle.

competitiveAnalysis.firstImpressions: The idea of actually walking to catch Pokémon is revolutionary, since the main line of games involves playing on your console and does not imply any physical activity. Even though the basic structure of the games provides a somewhat good experience regarding the online play and interacting with other people, Pokémon GO takes it to completely another level. The fact that you can meet people at Gyms to battle together in Raids gives players a unique experience. The main feature that makes this game attractive to audiences is the AR feature, which blends the reality with the game, making it fun to catch a Grass type Pokémon in your backyard or a Water type Pokémon when you're at the beach.
competitiveAnalysis.interactionNotes:
1. The "Dual-Layer" Interface (Navigation)
- Map layer vs Encounter layer
- the map is a standard 2D/3D abstraction of the real world
- the encounter layer switches to AR mode

2. The Pokéball Throw
- flick gesture; a high-frequency micro-interaction

3. Multi-Device Interaction
- The "Plus" wearable enhances the asynchronous play, by providing screenless interaction

4. Social & Spatial Presence 
- Raids, Lures placed on a Pokéstop facilitate meetups, by creating emergent social spaces while having awareness on the map about them.
competitiveAnalysis.accessibilityScore: Screen Reader Support (voice prompts), Visual Indicators for special Pokémon, Haptic Cues like vibration for when a Pokémon spawns close to you.
competitiveAnalysis.userFlowNotes:
The easiness depends on the ranking of the tasks. The core mechanic is exploration, which is improved by catching the Pokémon when you find them. Aside from this, there are multiple quests that you can complete, some are more difficult than others but they're fairly achievable. 

For most players that are unfamiliar with the franchise, the game offers a lot of tutorials and explanations which helps the user accommodate pretty fast with the mechanics of the game.
competitiveAnalysis.navigationNotes: Simple enough. Since the map is a rendering of the real-world map, it's pretty hard to get lost or to not be able to find a location. The game requires your device's internal GPS to move the character, which can be pretty buggy sometimes. All in all, it's quite good and it provides a experience that not only encourages you to explore more locations, but also doing it in a healthy way (Pokémon despawn early/fast if you try to play while in a car, for example, so you may not be able to catch them in time).
competitiveAnalysis.brandingNotes:
The Visual Identity is given by the digital-analog hybrid nature of the game, It bridges the gap between technology (like AR, wearables) and soft play. The UI uses a "simple nature" palette, primarily Sky Blue and Grass Green, thus reinforcing the idea of exploring in the nature. The iconography heavily relies on universally recognized symbols, for example the Pokéball icon serves as the button for the main menu.

Pokémon GO's core brand strategy is based on Strategic Familiarity. The game uses similar (or sometimes, exactly the same) sound effects and visual assets that were being used in the main line of the games (since 1990). This nostalgia + new tech formula works excellently for not only long-time fans, but also for newer players.
competitiveAnalysis.contentTone: The product communicates as an Encouraging Mentor: always focusing on the joy of exploration, while rarely punishing you for mistakes. The voice is a blend of Scientific Curiosity and Warm Encouragement, for example even if a rare Pokémon is nearby, the game doesn't use an aggressive language to catch your attention (like "HURRY!!!!") but instead provides light, passive alerts. Also, the text is designed for glanceability, by using verb-first instructions ("Spin the Photo Disc") and positive reinforcement through colorful visuals and encouraging words for completing different tasks.
competitiveAnalysis.strengths:
A major strength is the long-time fanbase of the Pokémon brand. Niantic knows very well how to "exploit" (in a positive way) it's users; it knows what the fanbase wants and how to satisfy them. Their marketing strategy is well done and many young adults feel nostalgia when thinking about Pokémon, which is why Pokémon GO had a big success.
The product convinced millions of people to increase their daily steps, which is a major component in our modern times. It encourages having a healthy lifestyle in a fun way.
The social presence markers (like Lures and Raids) provide a brilliant way to signal social activities happening in the real world, without necessarily relying on notifications or messages all the time.
The device interoperability is another good strength. Of course, there's the Pokémon GO Plus wearable, that allows users to play in a way that does not require having your eyes on the screen all the time, but there's more features that make the game enjoyable for hardcore fans. The app offers a fairly easy method of transferring Pokémon through other games, like from older or newer Nintendo consoles to Pokémon GO and vice-versa. It really is a big thing, since you can use your favorite caught Pokémon in battles across multiple games, and users provided an excellent feedback about this feature.
competitiveAnalysis.weaknesses:
Possibly one of the biggest weaknesses is the fact that the AR gimmick may drain battery faster or cause lag, many veteran players reporting they disabled the feature when playing. Micro-transactions are also annoying, even though the game offers you ways to progress (at a slower rate, to be honest), there are many problems related to the inventory management. In itself, the inventory space is pretty limited, so if you need a lot of space and fast, you might find yourself in a situation that involves real world currency.
Another problem is related to the usage of the screen, which we know can be damaging for the eyesight but not only that (headaches, dizziness, fatigue). It's kind of paradoxical when you think about it, a phone app that encourages sport but it also requires fixing your eyes on a screen. This can lead to other dangerous situations, like entering restricted areas without even noticing or injuring yourself in different ways because you don't pay attention to the physical world.

competitiveAnalysis.targetAudience: Persoane care joaca Dungeons and Dragons (kids-young adults)
competitiveAnalysis.firstImpressions:
It is designed to be quite straightforward, but it contains a large number of buttons for different resource pages. For tracking stats and resources, it is very effective and neatly encapsulates all the aspects that a game character has. The library with all the spells in the game, along with gameplay information, is well made and uses both images and text to clearly present what you need.

However, a downside is that the application feels heavy and cluttered with announcements and unnecessary elements, and it no longer seems focused on enhancing the gameplay itself, as it has become quite complicated.
competitiveAnalysis.interactionNotes: The interactivity is fairly good, but somewhat simplistic. Each piece of information is easy to find, although it may require pressing a few buttons to access it. However, I still consider it a bit cumbersome due to the large amount of information. One great feature is the dice rolling, which feels very lively and dynamic. Aside from that, the interaction is not very dynamic and feels mostly static.
competitiveAnalysis.accessibilityScore: For an inexperienced user, I would not consider it very easy to use, and for someone with poorer eyesight, the text is quite small, which I would see as a downside. However, for someone who is already familiar with the game and knows what resources they need, it works well.
competitiveAnalysis.userFlowNotes: At first, we are presented with the main page, which contains buttons leading to all the important sections that provide information and relatively helpful images about what we want to learn. After that, we can move on to the character creation section, where we can roll dice, add levels, and configure an entire character sheet, which I consider to be fairly complex.
competitiveAnalysis.navigationNotes: Navigation is, once again, quite straightforward and I think it does its job well. There is a search bar, as well as interactive images for each type of information when certain buttons are selected.
competitiveAnalysis.brandingNotes: From a branding perspective, the predominant colors are red and white, which are also the main colors in the game’s logo. The logo itself is a direct reference to the original game’s logo and is well complemented by images featuring characters and objects from the base game. Overall, it feels very professional and closely aligned with the tabletop game experience.
competitiveAnalysis.contentTone: The content is filled with small details that strongly evoke the game itself. The interface follows a predominantly medieval theme with a fantasy style that blends D&D elements, magic, and medieval features. For someone who is familiar with the genre and has played the game before, I would consider the theme to be appealing and familiar.
competitiveAnalysis.strengths: The interface provides all the information you need, the theme is very well suited, and it includes many elements from that universe. I especially like the highly detailed character creation feature, which presents the options step by step and provides helpful text for each choice, as well as the implemented dice rolling mechanic.
competitiveAnalysis.weaknesses: I consider the interface to be very heavy and cumbersome, and I would say that splitting the app into separate individual applications would be a major improvement: one app for learning, one for character data management, and another for the rest of the features currently included in the application.

userInterviews.discoveryNotes:
Student, pursuing a Master's degree.
Works at IBM, backend position. Favorite language is Java.
Hobbies: hiking, tabletop games, videogames. Favorite tabletop games: Dungeons & Dragons, Magic The Gathering
userInterviews.tasksAndActivities: Very organized and precise, has a structured timetable and plans ahead all of his tasks. Working in IT field made him develop a very algorithmic thinking, which helps a lot during boardgames and card games, topics that require quick and strategic decisions.
userInterviews.painPoints: The most frustrating part of having a job and pursuing a Master's degree is the limited free time. He misses meeting his friends weekly to play tabletop games, nowadays these occurrences are getting rarer. Also, some D&D campaigns take a very long time to finish, and they can't progress through it like before, precisely because each of his friends timetables.
userInterviews.opinions: Positive opinion about the app, thinks that it would facilitate interaction with his friends in an online environment. The AR features would "reignite the spark" about their D&D nights, offering a new and fun experience. He would like to have a feature that projects an AR map to a table, thus reducing the papers/cardboard needed.
userInterviews.pastExperiences: One important experience was discovering D&D Beyond, a site that lets you create a character, track various information and check all of the complicated rules. Basically, it is a helper/companion for the game. The downside is that it has paid plans, the free plan is not enough for an experienced D&D player and it can only serve as an introductory tool (if you don't buy the subscription).
userInterviews.futureProjections: A free app that works on donations and incorporates more devices than just laptop and smartphone. The app should also be automated (i.e. automatically increasing EXP Points when doing a quest, instead of manually adding them in your character sheet, real-time notifications during a campaign, daily mini-tasks to keep you engaged etc.).
userInterviews.additionalNotes: Amazed by the project idea, would 100% use the app in a real-life scenario.
